dossier.public_summary: The dip is clearly on the target star and looks flat-bottomed with no secondary or odd/even difference, but its depth triples between sectors from about 0.2% to 1% - a change that is confirmed to be real in the same TESS pipeline. Such sector-to-sector depth changes are inconsistent with a stable planet and point to stellar variability or a binary eclipse.

reasons.why: Depth changes catastrophically between sectors: 2358 ppm in sector 18, 3357 ppm in sector 58, 10745 ppm in sector 85 (depth_change_pct 152.9).
Depth change is real within TESS-SPOC, not a calibration difference: p_constant_all 4.707534212537934e-131 with only 3 sectors.
Strongly flat-bottomed favors planet, but a blended stellar eclipse can also be flat and duration ratio 1.575 is only consistent with inflated radius/ binary, not decisively planet-like.
Dip is on target (offset 0.6106 arcsec, 0.602 sigma) with neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0, so not a neighbour eclipse; depth change implicates variability or on-target binary over a quiet planet.
Lowest planet score reflects smoking-gun evidence above against a planet despite 5 similar checks that were planets.
